text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Since 2021, the Marrowfield Household Support Initiative has delivered monthly cash transfers to food-insecure families across the Tolven Valley. Women in each household receive the transfers, while village committees monitor distribution points. In the most recent lean season, 1,340 households received transfers of 45 dollars each, timed to coincide with the period when grain stocks typically run out. A baseline survey found that 62 percent of enrolled families were skipping at least one meal per day before joining the programme. Local markets did not experience price spikes after transfers began, which suggests that traders were able to meet the additional demand. However, the current funding cycle ends in March 2025, and no alternative source has yet been identified to sustain payments beyond that date. This proposal seeks support for a further two years of transfers.

passages.source_passage: During the third quarter of 2024, the Hollin Bridge Community Counselling Service held 412 individual sessions across its four drop-in centres. Counsellors referred clients to the district hospital when symptoms indicated a need for specialist care. Average scores on the wellbeing questionnaire improved by 18 percent between intake and the sixth session. Attendance at group sessions was lower than planned, with only nine of the fifteen scheduled groups reaching full capacity. Several clients reported that they did not feel comfortable attending sessions held in the village hall, citing concerns about being seen by neighbours. No serious adverse incidents were recorded during the period. The team recommends moving group meetings to the clinic annex from January.

passages.source_passage: Before your first household visit, make sure you understand how the borehole committees in Kessaru District operate. Each committee has seven members, and at least three of them must be women. Committees collect a fee of 200 shillings per household each month to pay for pump repairs. Do not promise families that latrine slabs will be provided free of charge, because the project subsidises only 60 percent of the cost. When you demonstrate handwashing, ask the caregiver to show the children the steps rather than doing it yourself. Remind families that a latrine should never be dug within 30 metres of the borehole. If a household refuses to participate, record the reason on your visit form and inform your supervisor.

passages.source_passage: The Brightwater Playgroup Network was founded in 2019 by a group of mothers in the hill settlements of Orenmoor. It now runs 23 weekly playgroups serving roughly 480 children under the age of five. Trained parent facilitators lead songs, storytelling and play activities that support early language and motor development. Most families in the area cannot afford formal preschool, and the nearest government early learning centre is more than 12 kilometres away. Until now, the network has not received any external funding; facilitators have contributed their time without pay. A 2023 assessment found that 71 percent of participating children met age-appropriate milestones, compared with 54 percent of a comparison group. Grant support would allow the network to train new facilitators and open playgroups in six additional villages.

passages.source_passage: As a community paralegal with the Ferncastle Justice Outreach Project, your role is to help people understand their rights, not to represent them in court. Most of the cases you will encounter involve land disputes, inheritance claims or unpaid wages. Last year, our 38 paralegals handled 2,150 enquiries, and about one in four was referred to a partner lawyer. Always explain the referral process to the client, and give the supervisor a written copy of the case notes. You should never charge a client for advice or accept gifts in return for assistance. If a client is in immediate danger, call the district coordinator before taking any further step. Keep all case notes in the locked cabinet at the outreach office, and do not take files home.

passages.source_passage: Rainfall in the Duskar Plateau has declined by roughly 20 percent since 1990, and the last three planting seasons have each ended in partial crop failure. Smallholder farmers in the area have traditionally grown maize, which does not tolerate long dry spells. In 2022, the Greenrow Resilience Trust introduced sorghum and cowpea varieties to 650 farming households on a trial basis. Yields from the drought-tolerant plots were nearly double those from neighbouring maize fields. Farmers were not initially willing to switch, largely because local traders offered lower prices for sorghum. The Trust responded by linking producer groups to two regional mills that now buy the grain at a guaranteed price. This proposal requests funding to extend the programme to a further 1,200 households.

passages.source_passage: By the end of June 2024, the Sallow Creek Savings Programme had established 64 village savings and loan groups with a combined membership of 1,520. Women make up 83 percent of members, and most groups meet weekly under a tree or in a church compound. Total savings reached 9.4 million kwacha, up from 6.1 million at the previous review. Loan repayment remained strong, although two groups in Ferrow ward reported members who had not repaid on time. Field officers did not record cases of cash going missing from lockboxes. Members used loans mainly to buy livestock, start small businesses or pay school fees. The share-out at the end of the cycle is scheduled for November.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, the Linden Hearth Family Service placed 57 children with approved foster families across the northern districts of Corvale. Our tracing officers reunited 31 separated children with parents or close relatives, an increase of 40 percent on the previous year. Every reunification was preceded by a home assessment and followed by at least three monitoring visits. Not all tracing efforts succeeded; in nine cases, no living relatives could be located despite extended searches. These children remain in long-term foster care, and none has been returned to residential institutions. Your funding allowed us to recruit two additional social workers in April, which reduced average caseloads from 35 to 22 children per worker.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the Amberly Evening Literacy Network. Classes run from 6 pm to 8 pm, four nights a week, in community halls and school classrooms. Most learners are adults who left school before completing grade three, and many work long hours during the day. Do not correct every mistake a learner makes aloud, as this can discourage people who are already anxious about reading. Begin each session by reviewing the previous lesson for about fifteen minutes. Learners should practise writing their own names and the names of family members in the first week. Keep a register of attendance; learners who miss more than five sessions in a row should receive a friendly home visit. No learner should ever be asked to pay for books or materials.

passages.source_passage: During 2024, the Nyakora District Health Partnership supported 146 community health workers serving roughly 58,000 people across the Ruvanga and Kiteme sub-counties. Each health worker visits an average of 25 households per month, screening children for malnutrition and referring pregnant women for antenatal care. Facility deliveries in the district rose from 61 percent to 74 percent over the year. Stock-outs of malaria test kits were a persistent problem, and health workers didn't receive replacement supplies for six weeks in the second quarter. Despite this, no maternal deaths were recorded among women enrolled in home visiting. We are grateful for your continued support, which funds monthly stipends and refresher training for all workers.
